intro: All three point toward a place, but each looks at a different part of the journey. に is the endpoint you arrive at. へ is the direction you head in. まで is the limit, 'as far as' or 'all the way to'. With 行く, 来る and 帰る, に and へ mean the same thing. The real choices are elsewhere: some verbs only take に, へ, not に, can go before の, and まで covers the whole distance.

skills.rule: Arriving or ending up somewhere takes に (or へ with go / come / return); heading that way takes へ; covering the distance up to a point, or stopping there, takes まで.
skills.explain:
Q1. Is the verb something other than movement: 会う, いる, ある, 住む? Then only に works. へ is never a substitute there.

Q2. Does the verb mean arriving or getting in or on: 着く, 入る, 乗る, 座る? Then に is the safe choice. へ also appears with 着く and 入る, but not with 乗る or 座る.

Q3. Does a noun follow, so you need の? Then へ: 母への手紙, 駅への道. にの is not possible. までの works only for a range: 駅までの道.

Q4. Is the verb 行く, 来る or 帰る? に and へ are both right. Use まで when you mean 'as far as' or 'the whole way'. 駅まで行きます suggests you stop or change there, and it is common with から: 東京から大阪まで.

Q5. Is it a verb of moving in a certain way, such as 歩く, 走る or 泳ぐ? Then まで: 駅まで歩きます. 駅に歩きます is wrong. If you want に, say 歩いて行きます.

For time, まで means 'until' and までに means 'by'.
patterns: [place] に / へ [行く / 来る / 帰る]
[place] に [着く / 入る / 乗る]
[place] まで [歩く / 走る / 送る]

examples.jp: 来週[らいしゅう]、京都[きょうと]{に}行[い]きます。
examples.en: I'm going to Kyoto next week.

examples.jp: 六時[ろくじ]に空港[くうこう]{に}着[つ]きました。
examples.en: We arrived at the airport at six.

examples.jp: 駅[えき]{まで}歩[ある]きましょう。
東京[とうきょう]から大阪[おおさか]{まで}新幹線[しんかんせん]で三時間[さんじかん]です。
examples.en: It's three hours from Tokyo to Osaka by bullet train.

examples.jp: 母[はは]{へ}の手紙[てがみ]を書[か]きました。
examples.en: I wrote a letter to my mother.

examples.jp: 駅[えき]{まで}送[おく]りますよ。
examples.en: I'll take you to the station.

contrast.note: に is the point you reach or end up at. It is the only choice with non-movement verbs, the natural one with arrival verbs such as 着く, and it cannot sit before の.
へ is the direction you head in. With 行く, 来る and 帰る it can replace に with no change in meaning. It cannot replace に for meeting, existence, boarding or time.
まで is the limit of the movement: 'as far as' or 'all the way to'. It is the natural choice with walking, running and seeing someone off, and it pairs with から.

mistakes.bad: 毎日[まいにち]駅[えき]{に}歩[ある]きます。
mistakes.good: 毎日[まいにち]駅[えき]{まで}歩[ある]きます。
mistakes.note: 歩く describes how you move, not where you arrive, so it needs まで (or 歩いて行く).

mistakes.bad: 友達[ともだち]{に}のプレゼントを買[か]いました。
mistakes.good: 友達[ともだち]{へ}のプレゼントを買[か]いました。
mistakes.note: Before の, use へ; にの is not Japanese.

mistakes.bad: 七時[しちじ]に駅[えき]{まで}着[つ]きました。
mistakes.good: 七時[しちじ]に駅[えき]{に}着[つ]きました。
mistakes.note: 着く is about arriving at a point, so it takes に.

skills.tip: End up there? に. Heading that way? へ. Covering the whole distance, or stopping at that point? まで.
